:::{#thm-outer-product-rank}
#### An outer product has rank one

If $\vecf{u}$ is a nonzero vector of length $m$
and $\vecf{v}$ is a nonzero vector of length $n$,
then $\operatorname{rank}(\vecf{u}\,\tp{\vecf{v}}) = 1$ (@def-rank).

:::

::: proof

Column $j$ of $\vecf{u}\,\tp{\vecf{v}}$ has entries $u_1 v_j, \ldots, u_m v_j$,
so it is the vector $v_j \vecf{u}$.

**The rank is at least one.**
Because $\vecf{v} \neq \vzero$, some entry $v_j$ is nonzero.
Then column $j$, $v_j \vecf{u}$, is a nonzero vector,
and a single nonzero vector is linearly independent (@def-linearly-independent):
$c\,(v_j \vecf{u}) = \vzero$ forces $c = 0$.

**The rank is at most one.**
Take any two columns $j \neq k$.
If

$$
\begin{aligned}
v_j &= v_k \\
&= 0,
\end{aligned}
$$

both columns are $\vzero$,
and $1 \cd (v_j \vecf{u}) + 1 \cd (v_k \vecf{u}) = \vzero$.
Otherwise, use the coefficients $c_j = v_k$ and $c_k = -v_j$,
which are not both zero:

$$
\ba
v_k\,(v_j \vecf{u}) - v_j\,(v_k \vecf{u})
&= (v_k v_j - v_j v_k)\,\vecf{u}
&& \text{(collect the scalar multiples of } \vecf{u} \text{)}
\\
&= 0 \cd \vecf{u}
&& \text{(multiplication of numbers is commutative)}
\\
&= \vzero
&& \text{(a zero multiple of a vector is } \vzero \text{)}
\ea
$$

Either way, every pair of columns has a combination
with coefficients that are not all zero and that equals $\vzero$.
Now take any set of two or more columns.
It contains a pair $j \neq k$.
Use that pair's coefficients for columns $j$ and $k$,
and the coefficient $0$ for every other column in the set.
This combination equals $\vzero$,
and its coefficients are not all zero,
so the set is not linearly independent (@def-linearly-independent).
The largest linearly independent set of columns therefore has one column.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-outer-product-rank}
#### The rank of an outer product

In @exm-outer-product,
the second column $(5, 10, 15)$ of $\vecf{u}\,\tp{\vecf{v}}$
is $\frac{5}{4}$ times the first column $(4, 8, 12)$,
because the columns are $v_1 \vecf{u} = 4\vecf{u}$ and $v_2 \vecf{u} = 5\vecf{u}$.
So the two columns are not linearly independent,
and the $3 \times 2$ matrix has rank $1$.

:::
